CLAUDE.md is the challenge brief, not our schema documentation, so I'll leave it as is. Now I want to double-check the order of my frontend edits versus when I ran the typecheck/lint, to make sure those changes were actually verified.

Tracing through the sequence, all the documents.tsx edits (the numberedSources helper, the sources section, and removing the section suffix) happened before the docker compose ps call and before running typecheck/lint, so everything's covered. Same for the backend.ts edits. I'll just run ReadLints on the edited files as a final sanity check rather than trying to set up a headless browser screenshot.

Fixed. The `[n]` markers in a saved brief were dead because `generated_citations` stored only the `chunk_id` and the template `section` — the number itself was thrown away at persist time, so the frontend had nothing to match `[3]` against. `MarkdownView` was already able to render a marker as a button; it just never found a citation with that marker and fell back to plain text.

What changed:

- **Schema**: new nullable `marker` column on `generated_citations` (migration `20260918180000_citation_marker`). Nullable so briefs generated before today keep their evidence rows instead of getting a fake number.
- **Backend** (`apps/backend/src/common/services/backend.ts`): the brief writer now saves the marker it already extracted from the markdown, and `getDocument` returns it on each citation, ordered by marker.
- **Frontend** (`apps/frontend/src/pages/documents.tsx`): markers in the body are now clickable and open the passage drawer, and a numbered **Sources** footnote sits under the brief listing each marker with its filename, organisation, and passage number (deduped, since one marker can be cited under several headings).

Verified by generating a fresh Cascade Care Group brief through the API: the body cites markers 1, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7, 8, 10 and every one of them resolves to a stored citation, with no unmatched markers. `make typecheck`, `make lint`, and `make test` (49 tests) all pass. Two notes: that verification run left a new PC2 brief in your local database, and the older PC1 brief predates the migration, so its markers stay inert until you regenerate it.

I also updated `API_SPECS.md` and `DATABASE_SCHEMA.md` (they previously said generate sets no marker), added a reminder bullet to `DECISIONS.md` quoting your request, and refreshed the memory files — including the "blocked on Anthropic credits" known issue, which is no longer true now that generation runs end to end.

Those errors are pre-existing and environmental, not caused by my change, and Docker lint passed. I should note this trust-surface refinement follows an explicit instruction and is logged in DECISIONS.md, mention that the old PC1 brief needs regeneration to show clickable markers, and flag that I generated a PC2 brief during verification which created data in their database worth telling them about.
